subject: Concurrency & Latency Profiling — detailed methodology and scaling playbook
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@octane-sys.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: detailed concurrency & latency profiling for RFP

Jordan —

Thanks for taking this on. As part of Octane Systems' RFP we need a detailed, repeatable benchmarking methodology and sample results that demonstrate how Redwood behaves under concurrent request load and mixed traffic. Specifically we need: 

- Test methodology: driver type, warmup, measurement windows, and any variance controls.
- Workloads: short-chat (avg 60 tokens), long completion (avg 600 tokens), embeddings (1k vectors), and multi-turn chat with 8-turn context.
- Concurrency sweep: from 1 to 500 concurrent connections; sustained (30m) vs burst (2m) profiles.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (generation-only and end-to-end), tokens/sec throughput, GPU utilization, CPU/network stats, error/retry rates.
- Scaling behavior: how throughput/latency change as we add replicas; any known non-linearities (KV-cache saturation, batching thresholds).
- Test environment: typical HW variants (A100/H100), quantized vs FP16, model sizes tested.

Can you provide: a) a repeatable methodology doc and b) a small set of representative results (CSV or spreadsheet) we can include in the RFP appendix by Feb 14?

Also share any constraints or caveats (e.g., caching assumptions, batching heuristics) we should call out.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Senior Procurement Manager
Octane Systems

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@octane-sys.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: detailed concurrency & latency profiling for RFP

Alex —

Appreciate the clear ask. We're on it and can deliver a reproducible methodology plus an initial results package by Feb 14. Attached is a short outline of our profiling approach (initial-profiling-outline.pdf) — the high-level plan below. We'll also need a representative sample of your production traffic (anonymized payload sizes, token distributions, and concurrency mix) to run a best-effort mirror; if that's not available we'll use a conservative synthetic workload.

High-level profiling plan (summary):
- Driver: k6 with a custom Redwood load-driver (open-source) + native gRPC harness for high-concurrency measurement.
- Warmup: phased warmup (10m low-concurrency, 10m ramp to target) to populate prefix/KV caches.
- Measurement windows: 30m sustained windows and 3 x 2m burst windows at peak concurrency.
- Metrics collected: request latency (client-observed generation start/finish), tokens/sec, batch sizes, server-side token-emit timing, GPU utilization, mem / KV cache hit rates, and tail latencies (p95/p99).
- Variance control: repeat each test 3x and report median and interquartile range; control for preemption by pinning instance types where possible.
- Scaling matrix: run on 1,2,4,8,16 replica configs (replica = GPU instance) to show non-linear regimes (batching thresholds, KV cache pressure).
- Models & HW: test with mediums (13B) and larges (70B) on H100 and A100; run quantized variants (8-bit) where supported for cost/latency trade-offs.

Open question: do you want us to include warm-cache and cold-cache curves separately? Warm-cache (prefix caching) is where we expect the best cost/latency economics; cold-cache shows worst-case tail behavior.

Proposed next steps:
1) Share sample payloads or confirm synthetic approach by Feb 4.
2) We run micro-sweeps and return a draft workbook by Feb 10.
3) Finalized workbook + methodology + attachments by Feb 14.

Looping in Karthik/Marissa/Dev for runbook details and to own the test execution.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi team —

FW: Octane RFP asks below. Key asks: concurrency sweep to 500, sustained vs burst, p50/p95/p99, and scaling matrix across 1-16 replicas. They want a repeatable methodology and a small result set by Feb 14.

Dev — can you run a directed sweep with our internal harness on H100 (x2) and A100 (x2) across these model families: 13B (fp16), 13B (int8), 70B (fp16). Deliverables: 1) load-sweep-results.csv with per-step stats (concurrency, p50/p95/p99, throughput, batch size distribution, GPU util), 2) latency-profiles.json sampling tail-cases, 3) short notes on observed non-linearities and caching effects. Aim to reuse the 'workload: chat-short (60 tokens) & chat-long (600 tokens)' profiles. Keep runs reproducible (seeded randomness).

Karthik — please help define the test matrix (replica counts and schedule) and own the warmup policy. Marissa — flag any security/data handling caveats (if we ask for payloads) before we request sample data.

I expect initial artifacts by EOD Feb 10. Let me know blockers.

Jordan
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2027 16:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: detailed concurrency & latency profiling for RFP

Team —

I ran the directed sweeps on H100 and A100 across the requested model variants. Deliverables attached: load-sweep-results.csv and latency-profiles.json (trimmed). Summary highlights:

- Environment: 4x H100 per replica (multi-GPU config with NCCL), instances pinned, driver = k6 native gRPC harness.
- Warm-cache vs cold-cache: warm-cache p95 improved by ~30% across the board compared to cold-cache for chat-short; long completions saw ~20% p95 improvement. Cold-cache runs show significant p99 spikes during first 30s as KV cache warms.
- Concurrency regimes: up to ~80 concurrent connections we observe near-linear throughput gains; between 80–320 we see sublinear returns due to batching thresholds and increased KV cache pressure; beyond ~320 we hit GPU-side scheduling contention and p99 tails increase sharply.
- Quantization (int8) reduced median latency by ~18% and increased throughput ~25% for 13B. For 70B, quantization help was smaller (~10%) but more variable (increased variance at high concurrency).
- Example numbers (13B, H100, warm-cache, chat-short): concurrency 1 -> p95 45ms; 50 -> p95 120ms; 200 -> p95 290ms; 400 -> p95 760ms; p99 at 400 ~1.9s. Throughput tokens/sec scaled roughly linearly until 200 concurrency then flattened.

Caveats / notes:
- Our public-hosted environment adds a layer of routing that can add ~5–10ms overhead relative to private deploys; we can run isolated lab tests for a lower baseline if Octane prefers.
- Batching heuristics are workload dependent; real-world multi-tenant noise can affect variance.
- We sampled a small set of payload shapes; full production traffic may shift the precise thresholds.

Attachments: load-sweep-results.csv (per-step stats), latency-profiles.json (sampled traces). I also exported a short workbook draft. If this looks good I'll stitch into a final workbook and methodology doc for Jordan to send externally.

- Dev

Date: Mon, 14 Feb 2027 11:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: detailed concurrency & latency profiling for RFP

Alex / Sanjay / Procurement team —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is our consolidated profiling package for the RFP appendix: redwood-perf-workbook.xlsx, initial-profiling-outline.pdf (methodology), and the raw artifacts (load-sweep-results.csv, latency-profiles.json). High-level summary and caveats below.

Executive summary (short):
- Method: repeatable k6/gRPC-driven harness; phased warmup; 30m sustained windows + 3x2m bursts; tests run 3x and medians reported.
- Observed behavior: near-linear throughput until ~80–200 concurrency (workload dependent); beyond that batching and KV cache pressure produce sublinear throughput gains and increased tail. Tail p99 growth becomes significant past 320 concurrent connections on H100 in our lab runs.
- Quantization: int8 gives meaningful median latency and throughput improvements for 13B; gains reduce at 70B and variance increases at high concurrency.
- Representative numbers (13B, H100, warm-cache, chat-short): p50~22–35ms, p95~120–290ms (depending on concurrency), p99 up to ~1.9s at extreme concurrency. See workbook for full matrix.

Caveats and recommended mitigations:
- Warm vs cold cache: warm-cache performance is materially better; recommend a warmup policy or sticky routing for production traffic that benefits from prefix/KV caching.
- Autoscaling recommendation: scale on queue-length + observed p95 rather than raw CPU to capture model-side throughput changes.
- Fallbacks: configure model-variant fallbacks (smaller family / quantized) for burst periods to reduce tail exposure.

Next steps we propose:
1) If you can provide a small anonymized sample of production payloads (token lengths & concurrency mix), we will re-run and supply a final, customer-specific workbook.
2) If Octane prefers isolated lab baselines (no routing overhead), we can run on dedicated private infra and provide adjusted numbers.

Attached files and links: redwood-perf-workbook.xlsx, initial-profiling-outline.pdf, load-sweep-results.csv, latency-profiles.json, mutual-action-plan.docx. Public workbook link: https://redwood.example.com/workbooks/OCT-2027-1182-perf

Happy to run a walk-through of the workbook next week — propose Tue Feb 16 or Wed Feb 17. What time works for you?

Best,
Jordan Blake
